intro.title: Nesting (@nest / &)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple card component with a header and body, using CSS nesting to style its inner elements without repeating selectors. You'll learn the core concept of nesting, which allows you to write cleaner, more organized CSS by placing child selectors inside their parent rules. The main technologies involved are the CSS nesting syntax, including the `&` symbol for parent reference and the `@nest` at-rule for more complex nesting patterns. This beginner-friendly approach helps you understand how to structure styles hierarchically, making your CSS easier to read and maintain.
intro.usecase: CSS nesting is a fundamental pattern for styling complex, component-based interfaces like dashboards, admin panels, and design systems. For example, developers use nesting to style all interactive states (hover, focus, active) of a button within a single rule block, or to target specific elements inside a modal or card component without repeating selectors. This keeps styles modular, readable, and maintainable, especially when working with frameworks like React or Vue where UI is built from nested components. It's essential for efficiently styling forms, navigation menus, and data tables where visual hierarchy and state management are critical.

objectives: Apply the & selector to style nested elements within a parent selector
Construct CSS rules using @nest to target specific descendant relationships
Configure nested selectors to override inherited styles from parent elements
Implement nesting to organize related styles within a single rule block
Manipulate nested selectors to create hover and focus states for child elements
Integrate nesting with pseudo-classes to style elements based on their parent state
Update existing CSS code by refactoring flat selectors into nested structures

steps.title: Introduce the & (Ampersand) Selector
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a .card element that uses the & selector to target .card:hover and change the background color to lightblue.
steps.hint: Inside the .card rule, nest a rule using &:hover to apply styles when the card is hovered.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .card rule should include a nested &:hover selector that changes the background color.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a .card rule with a nested &:hover selector that sets background-color: lightblue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the & selector inside the .card rule to target .card:hover and set background-color: lightblue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS doesn't include the required nested &:hover rule. Remember to use & to reference the parent selector when nesting.

steps.title: Apply Basic Nesting with &
steps.instruction: Inside the .card rule, nest a rule for .card-title using the & selector to create a descendant selector.
steps.hint: Use the & selector followed by a space and .card-title to target elements with class 'card-title' that are inside elements with class 'card'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .card rule will contain a nested .card-title rule using the & selector, creating a descendant selector relationship.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .card rule with a nested & .card-title rule inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the & selector followed by a space and .card-title inside the .card rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the .card rule, use & .card-title to create a nested rule for elements with class 'card-title' inside elements with class 'card'.

steps.title: Nest Pseudo-classes with &
steps.instruction: Inside the .card selector, add a nested rule for the :hover pseudo-class using the & selector. The rule should change the background color to lightblue when the card is hovered.
steps.hint: Use &:hover { background-color: lightblue; } inside the .card selector. The & refers to the parent selector .card.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .card selector now includes a nested :hover pseudo-class that changes the background color to lightblue on hover.
successCriteria: The .card selector contains a nested &:hover rule with background-color: lightblue;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct syntax. The &:hover rule should be nested inside .card with the background-color property set to lightblue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't include the required nested pseudo-class rule. Inside .card, add &:hover { background-color: lightblue; } using the & selector.

steps.title: Use & for Compound Selectors
steps.instruction: Inside the .card rule, create a compound selector that targets elements with both the .card and .highlight classes by adding a nested rule for &.highlight.
steps.hint: Use the & symbol followed directly by .highlight to create a selector that matches .card.highlight.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .card rule will have a nested &.highlight selector that can be used to style .card.highlight elements.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a nested &.highlight selector inside the .card rule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the & symbol correctly. It should be followed directly by .highlight without any space to create the compound selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember that compound selectors like .card.highlight can be created in nested CSS by using & followed directly by the class name.

steps.title: Introduce @nest for Complex Nesting
steps.instruction: Add a rule inside the .card selector that uses @nest to target .card-title elements that are direct children of .card (using the & selector).
steps.hint: Use @nest when you need to place the parent selector (&) somewhere other than the beginning of a nested selector. For example: @nest .parent & { ... }
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will contain a @nest rule inside .card that demonstrates complex nesting where the parent selector (&) is placed in the middle of a selector.
successCriteria: The .card selector contains a valid @nest rule that uses & to target .card-title elements that are direct children of .card.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your @nest rule is correctly formatted and placed inside the .card selector. The syntax should be: @nest .card > & .card-title { ... }
steps.feedbackWrong: The @nest rule is missing or incorrect. Remember that @nest is used when you need to place the parent selector (&) somewhere other than the beginning of a nested selector. Try adding: @nest .card > & .card-title { ... } inside the .card selector.

steps.title: Apply @nest for Advanced Nesting
steps.instruction: Inside the .card rule, complete the @nest rule by adding a declaration that sets the color property to 'darkblue' for the .card-title when it's a direct child of .card.
steps.hint: The @nest rule should target .card > & .card-title. Add a color property inside that rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The @nest rule will apply a dark blue color to .card-title elements that are direct children of .card, demonstrating how @nest handles complex selector patterns.
successCriteria: The @nest .card > & .card-title rule contains a color: darkblue; declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the color property inside the @nest rule with the value 'darkblue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @nest rule should contain a color declaration. Try adding 'color: darkblue;' inside the @nest .card > & .card-title rule.

steps.title: Review and Practice Nesting Concepts
steps.instruction: Complete the CSS example by adding a hover effect to the .card selector using the & nesting operator.
steps.hint: Inside the .card rule, use &:hover to change the background color when hovering.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .card selector will have a hover effect that changes its background color, demonstrating the & nesting operator.
successCriteria: The .card rule contains a &:hover selector that changes the background color.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you added the &:hover selector inside the .card rule and changed the background color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect is missing or incorrect. Check that you used &:hover inside .card and set a background color.
